Bennett made the announcement in a blog post . In the post, she shared that it was a decision she grappled with for many months. " We have made such great progress in the last few years and serving the residents of District 2 is something that I deeply treasure. As someone with deep-rooted principles in community, I am holding space for bittersweet acknowledgement of the feeling of pride for the work that has been completed, responsibility for what is left unfinished, and releasing that responsibility to the faith I have in the next cohort of leaders," Bennett wrote. She continued by stating, " I am carrying extremely heavy buckets that warrant my attention. I very much look forward to spending quality time with my dad, transitioning to the next step in my commitment to public service, and finally getting to just be 25-years-old." Download the 27 New Now app and 27 Storm Track app here Madison Alder responds to resolution to censure him MADISON (WKOW) — A Madison alder who has come under scrutiny for his alleged conduct toward another alder is pushing back. Several Madison alders and the mayor recently sponsored a resolution to censure Alder Charles Myadze for "conduct unbecoming of an alder." According to a filing on the city's website, the resolution cites "concerning actions" by Alder Myadze documented in an investigative report. The resolution claims the findings in that report "undermined confidence in [Myadze's] ability to maintain the professional decorum expected of a public official." It cites an April 2022 incident accusing Myadze of creating a hostile work environment. Alder Juliana Bennett said in a blog post that Myadze cornered her in his car and threatened her. In a statement to 27 News, Myadze described the communication he had with Bennett at that time as "professional." Myadze responded to the investigation in a blog post published Saturday night. Myadze said in part, "I will acknowledge that I am not a perfect man and offer my sincere and public apology for any unease or discomfort that I may have unintentionally caused. That was never my intent." He added, "I find this whole censure process to be disruptive to the collaborative and respectful environment necessary for the work of the people. I am committed to doing the work of the city and representing my constituents to the best of my ability. I oppose this censure resolution on the merit of the findings of a thorough investigation by the City and its hired counsel, and it is my hope that we can move beyond this together, for the good people of Madison." Myadze pointed to a chain of text messages that he said dispute the allegations that he attempted to silence Alder Bennett. "There are 90 text messages between Alder Juliana Bennett and myself," Myadze said. "I have provided a small handful of the text messages as evidence showing that I did not silence Alder Juliana Bennett, and she did not keep her distance from me as she alleged as of April 7, 2022." In one message exchange from the fall of 2022, Myadze said he complimented Juliana's work and she replied, “Fs love. Gotta support each other and what’s right.” Myadze concluded by saying the messages "illustrate the nature of our interactions, which I believe I was professional and cordial. It is my hope that sharing these will help bring clarity and context to this matter." You can read Myadze's full response here . Send breaking news tips to news@wkow.com . Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. && Close Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save 'Please reconsider your decision': Madison Common Council censures, removes alder from committees Dec 10, 2024 Dec 10, 2024 Updated Dec 10, 2024 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save MADISON (WKOW) — The Madison Common Council voted Tuesday night to censure District 18 Alder Charles Myadze, as well as to remove and replace him from the committees on which he serves. The decision comes after three women accused Myadze of sexual harassment and domestic violence. The City of Madison opened an investigation into his behavior, however it found insufficient evidence that he violated the city's policy on discrimination and harassment. One of the women who came forward with these accusations was Juliana Bennett, another Madison alder. She shared her experiences with Myadze in a November blog post. Since then, not only was the investigation launched but the resolution to censure him was introduced. Juliana's dad, James Bennett, spoke at the podium during Tuesday night's council meeting, where he got emotional. "Not just because my daughter is here, who's my seventh child. When we came to Madison in 2017, I was against her being on City Council. I thought that being here she should at least be in a safe environment. When I see that she isn't in a safe environment, I fought myself. I let her down. I let my family down," he said. A majority of people who registered to speak were in agreement with the resolution. However there were some who were not. They said a council floor is no place for due justice and challenge the accusations made against Alder Myadze. "I humbly pray that you please reconsider your decision. As an alder, I can go to any committee. I've gone to committees I don't even serve on. Whether that be the finance committee, whether that might be any committee. Just to be able to serve my constituents," Myadze said before the council voted to remove him from his committee assignments. Myadze has denied all of the accusations. He said in a statement that he does not believe his actions have reflected poorly on the council, nor have they diminished public trust.
